items.title: Builder execution boundary
rules: Read and edit only the admitted isolated checkout and task-owned context.
On Windows PowerShell 5.1, every textual `Get-Content` read must use `-Encoding UTF8`; never rewrite source from mojibake console text.
Do not publish, install, activate, or mutate canonical workspace source; the trusted worker owns validation and Trial delivery.

items.title: Skill WebUI and public tool contract
rules: For every added or changed same-skill WebUI `callSkill`, skill `dataSource`, or handler callable, reconcile the exact name across `webui.json`, `skill.yaml` `tools`, `exports.tools`, the entry/`@tool` handler, and complete input/output schemas in the same patch.

Do not conclude while a callable exists in code or UI but is absent from the public manifest graph. If a required counterpart is outside the authorized paths, stop and report that scope blocker instead of leaving a partial contract.
Browser-read tools require a bounded declared `data_route`; action acknowledgements stay compact and do not duplicate projected data. Keep duplicated skill/scenario UI contracts in parity.

items.title: Declarative UI state and identity
rules: Use stable unique IDs and canonical language-neutral refs for areas, widgets, actions, and domain targets; localized labels are presentation, never routing or storage identity.
Represent materially different page modes with `layout.variants`, and update the view mode plus selected identity atomically; do not stack competing main areas behind incidental visibility checks.
Preserve established interaction state and unrelated behavior. Dynamic IDs, renderer-private assumptions, and hidden client-only state are contract defects.

items.title: Scenario composition boundary
rules: A scenario orchestrates skills, surfaces, NLU affordances, and bindings; do not hide reusable capability, external IO, long-running work, heavy state, or new permissions inside scenario data.

Declare required and optional skill dependencies and bind actions to real exported tools. Missing required capability blocks apply; missing optional capability needs an explicit degraded or guided-install state.
Keep scenario-owned state separate from skill-owned domain state, and do not let Prototype or Preview install, activate, or mutate live runtime.

items.title: Data route and receiver ownership
rules: Declare receiver ownership, route budget, causal read policy, and projection target explicitly.
Do not use Yjs as an unconstrained database or publish duplicate state through action responses and projections.
A route or projection mismatch is a validation failure, not a reason to add an undeclared fallback.

items.title: Causal tool-backed reads
rules: A tool-backed browser surface names the exact tool and a finite causal `read_policy`: semantic read key, allowed triggers, invalidation tags, rate budget, and last-value behavior.
Do not turn rerenders, unrelated actions, focus, generic state updates, or timers into reads. Explicit Retry reloads only the selected semantic read identity.
Keep the last valid value only when declared, and distinguish loading, stale, unavailable, permission-denied, and domain-empty states.

items.title: Typed resource and storage boundary
rules: Use typed AdaOS resource/provider contracts and owner-scoped SDK storage roots.
Do not let callers choose arbitrary filesystem roots or persist synthetic provider data as authoritative state.
CRUD and reload behavior must preserve revision, authorization, and deterministic empty/unavailable states.

items.title: Runtime lifecycle and failure evidence
rules: Keep activation, rehydrate, drain, and failure paths bounded, idempotent, and observable.
Validation and runtime failures must produce stable error codes, trace/retryability metadata, and bounded evidence; do not hide them behind synthetic success defaults or domain-empty UI.
A command acknowledgement is not proof that browser-visible state was delivered or that the selected runtime slot loaded the new handler.

items.title: Python import, dependency, and resource lifecycle
rules: Keep imports passive: no threads, model loads, sockets, subscriptions, external callbacks, publishes, or persistent writes at module import time.
Bound every cache and worker by items/bytes/time, give every thread, task, executor, subprocess, model, and callback one lifecycle owner plus drain/dispose cleanup, and keep reload idempotent.
Declare every imported dependency and its supported isolation boundary in `skill.yaml`; validate against the authoritative manifest schema instead of relying on Builder's environment.

items.title: Conversation, localization, and Pending Actions
rules: Keep user-visible text in declared localization contracts and preserve UTF-8 input exactly.
Conversational ambiguity requires bounded clarification; it must not silently change the requested action or enter Builder planning.
Use governed Pending Actions for consequential confirmation and preserve channel-neutral semantics across UI, voice, and Telegram.

items.title: Root-accounted asynchronous LLM work
rules: Submit long or Builder-like model work through the Root-accounted async LLM job SDK, persist its job_id, and resume by polling; use synchronous calls only for bounded short work.
Validate model output against the admitted schema before applying it, and retain provider usage and failure evidence for Subscription accounting.
Do not call model providers directly or introduce an unmetered fallback path.

items.title: Member and subnet-aware handling
rules: Derive member and device identity from trusted event or routing metadata; never accept caller-selected ownership or hardcode the local node.
Bound per-receiver payload and subnet fanout, and represent dormant, disconnected, partial, and stale member data explicitly.
Coalesce high-frequency membership updates and keep handlers idempotent across reconnect and replay.

items.title: Exact consumer and SDK contract realization
rules: Treat admitted operation names and request/response schemas as ABI: implement and export every exact required operation, including required/const/enum/additionalProperties boundaries.
Prove compatibility through the real published consumer normalizer, validator, or conformance path; a self-authored look-alike fixture is not consumer evidence.
When the public SDK/API cannot express the requirement, do not patch around core or imitate the contract locally; return the governed core-capability escalation.
